title: Russell: percepts are physical events in the percipient’s brain

statements.text: Percepts are part of the matter of the percipient’s brain. They are not known to have any intrinsic character that physical events cannot have, so there is no ground for excluding them from the physical world, and several reasons for including them.

sources.quote: these percepts are really part of the matter of the percipient’s brain
are not known to have any intrinsic character which physical events cannot have
I conclude, then, that there is no good ground for excluding percepts from the physical world, but several strong reasons for including them.
